# **II. Software Requirement Specification** {#ii.-software-requirement-specification}

## **1\. Overall Requirements** {#1.-overall-requirements}

### **1.1 Context Diagram** {#1.1-context-diagram}

The School Administration and Workflow Platform for Primary Schools (SAWP) is a web-based system for routine primary-school administration. It connects Parent / Guardian, Homeroom Teacher, Giáo vụ, Lunch Service Staff, School Board, and System Administrator through one role-based platform. SAWP begins after a student is already enrolled in the school and supports centralized student records, class placement and schedules, daily attendance, daily school-lunch registration, administrative requests, notifications, auditability, and operational reporting.

Scope boundary: Admissions/enrollment, school transportation, grading/academic assessment, homework/online learning, payroll, full accounting, library management, and inventory management are outside the baseline SAWP scope. School lunch means daily meal registration and operational meal counts; it does not represent a full day-boarding management module.

### **1.3 User Requirements** {#1.3-user-requirements}

#### ***1.3.1 Actors***

| \# | Actor | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Guest | Users who access the system without logging in.  |
| 2 | Parent / Guardian  | Register services and track results. Access is restricted to their own applications and verified linked children only.  |
| 3 | Homeroom Teacher  | Review relevant leave and transfer requests, and view class service information. Access is limited to assigned classes and specifically assigned cases.  |
| 4 | Office Staff | Operate admissions, records and school services based on their assigned department and workflow responsibilities.  |
| 5 | Services Staff  | Staff handling student and school support services.  |
| 6 | Email Service  | An external email dispatch service (SMTP) used by SAWP. It handles automated account verification emails, password reset requests, and system notifications. |
| 7 | School Board | School leadership responsible for authorized or escalated decisions, including designated leave and class-transfer approvals, and for reviewing school-wide operational dashboards/reports and announcements within their authority. |
| 8 | System Administrator  | Manage accounts, permissions, templates and workflow configuration. Technical privileges do not automatically grant business approval authority.  |

#### ***1.4.4 Non-UI Functions***

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Authentication & Session Security | Session Validation and Expiration | Validates each protected request, enforces inactivity expiration, and invalidates sessions after logout, account deactivation, password change, or administrator-assisted reset. |
| 2 | Authorization | Role and Data-Scope Authorization Filter | Applies role, linked-child, assigned-class, and feature permissions before reading or mutating protected data. |
| 3 | Auditability | Audit Event Recorder | Creates append-only audit events for security-sensitive and material administrative changes, including actor, timestamp, entity/action, and relevant before/after references. |
| 4 | Workflow | Administrative Request Routing Engine | Routes leave, class-transfer, and school-document requests to the correct role according to request type/status and records every transition. |
| 5 | Notifications | In-System Notification Dispatcher | Creates recipient-specific notifications from workflow events, announcements, and important operational changes and maintains per-recipient read state. |
| 6 | Attendance | Attendance Lock and Consistency Validator | Prevents duplicate student/day records, enforces Homeroom Teacher class scope, and applies the teacher edit window and Giáo vụ correction rules. |
| 7 | Lunch Service | Lunch Cutoff and Meal Count Service | Validates daily registration/cancellation cutoff and service-day availability, then recalculates meal counts after each valid change. |
| 8 | School Calendar | School-Day Validation Service | Provides school-day/holiday information to attendance, leave, schedule, and lunch modules using the active school year and school timezone. |
| 9 | Data Import | Student Import Validator | Parses supported import files, validates required fields and uniqueness, previews row-level errors, and commits only confirmed valid rows. |
| 10 | Reporting | Operational Report Aggregator | Aggregates role-authorized student/class, attendance, lunch, and administrative-request metrics without exposing out-of-scope data. |
| 11 | History | Historical Record Preservation | Keeps class assignment, request status, lunch, attendance, and audit history accessible after current records change or a school year is archived. |
| 12 | File Handling | Attachment Validation and Storage | Validates allowed file type/size, stores approved attachments, and enforces access permission when files are retrieved. |

#### ***1.4.5 Entity Relationship Diagram***

![][image16]

#### ***1.4.6 Logical ERD Diagram***

![][image17]

**Entities Description**

| \# | Entity | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | User | User login account, status, credential/security metadata, and linkage to operational profile. |
| 2 | Role | Defined SAWP roles such as Parent / Guardian, Homeroom Teacher, Giáo vụ, Lunch Service Staff, Ban Giám hiệu, and System Administrator. |
| 3 | Permission | Granular authorization capability assigned to roles. |
| 4 | UserRole | Associative entity linking users to roles when more than one role is supported. |
| 5 | StaffProfile | School staff identity used for teacher/administrative role linkage. |
| 6 | Guardian | Parent/guardian identity and contact information. |
| 7 | Student | Central record for a student already enrolled in the school. |
| 8 | StudentGuardian | Relationship between Student and Guardian, including relationship type and primary-contact flag. |
| 9 | SchoolYear | School-year name, start/end dates, and active/archive state. |
| 10 | SchoolCalendarDay | A date within a school year marked as school day, holiday, or exceptional closure. |
| 11 | Class | Class name, grade, school year, capacity, and status. |
| 12 | HomeroomAssignment | Effective-dated assignment of a Homeroom Teacher to a Class. |
| 13 | ClassAssignment | Effective-dated assignment of a Student to a Class, preserving history. |
| 14 | ClassSchedule | Weekly/dated schedule entries for a Class. |
| 15 | AttendanceRecord | Daily attendance status for one Student on one school day. |
| 16 | LeaveRequest | Leave/absence request details associated with an AdministrativeRequest. |
| 17 | LunchServiceDay | Daily lunch availability and registration/cancellation cutoff. |
| 18 | LunchRegistration | Student lunch registration for one service date and its active/cancelled/corrected state. |
| 19 | AdministrativeRequest | Common request header: requester, student, type, status, timestamps, and assignee/processing data. |
| 20 | RequestStatusHistory | Chronological status transitions and processing notes for an AdministrativeRequest. |
| 21 | RequestAttachment | File metadata linked to an AdministrativeRequest. |
| 22 | ClassTransferDetail | Class-transfer-specific information linked one-to-one to an AdministrativeRequest. |
| 23 | DocumentRequestDetail | School-document-request-specific information linked one-to-one to an AdministrativeRequest. |
| 24 | IssuedDocument | Metadata about a school document issued in response to an approved request. |
| 25 | Notification | Recipient-specific in-system notification and read state. |
| 26 | Announcement | School announcement content, target audience, and publish schedule/status. |
| 27 | AuditLog | Append-only security/administrative action record. |

#### ***2.1.1 UC-01 Login System***

##### **a. Screen Layouts** 

**UC-01 screen layout**

![][image18] 

##### **b. Specification**

| Use Case Name: | UC-01 Login  |  |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary Actor:** | Guest | **Secondary Actors:** | None |
| **Description:** | Authenticates an active user and directs the user to the workspace permitted by their role. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow** | N1. Login System 1\. User opens the Login page. 2\. User enters their username/email and password, then submits the request.  3\. System validates the submitted credentials. (E1) 4\. System verifies the account status. (E2) 5\. System identifies the user's role, creates an authenticated session, and redirects the user to the corresponding role dashboard. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1. Authenticated User Access: If a currently authenticated user accesses the Login page, the system immediately redirects the user to their current role dashboard.  |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | E1. Invalid Credentials: If the username/email and password combination is incorrect, the system displays MSG02 and remains on the Login page. E2. Inactive Account: If the account is inactive, disabled, or locked, the system displays MSG03 and denies access. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-01, BR-03, BR-05, BR-48 |  |  |

| **Normal Flow** | N1. Submit Class Transfer Request 1\. Parent selects a linked child and opens Class Transfer Request. 2\. Parent enters reason and optional preferred target class/supporting attachment. 3\. System validates required information and active duplicate requests. (E1) 4\. Parent submits the request. 5\. System creates the request in Submitted status and notifies Office Staff. 6\. System displays MSG30. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1. Parent submits without a preferred class; Office Staff may propose an available class during review. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | E1. Another active transfer request exists or attachment is invalid \-\> display MSG09/MSG41. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-34, BR-35, BR-37, BR-50 |  |  |

 

#### ***2.6.2 UC-37 Review Class Transfer Request***

##### **a. Screen Layouts**

| **Normal Flow** | N1. Review Class Transfer Request 1\. Office Staff opens a submitted transfer request. 2\. System displays student, current class, reason, class capacities, and attachments. 3\. Office Staff checks completeness and feasible target classes. 4\. Office Staff records review notes and a recommended target class if applicable. 5\. Office Staff forwards the request to School Board for decision or rejects it when administratively invalid according to policy. 6\. System updates status/history and notifies relevant users. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flows:** | A1. Request more information from parent \-\> status remains open and parent is notified. |  |  |
| **Exceptions:** | E1. No eligible target class is available \-\> display MSG15 and keep request under review. |  |  |
| **Business Rules:** | BR-35, BR-37, BR-41, BR-42 |  |  |

School Board approves or rejects and enters an optional decision note. 4\. System records the decision and status history. 5\. System notifies Parent / Guardian and Office Staff using MSG31 or MSG32. |  |  |

Office Staff confirms target class and effective date. 4\. System rechecks class capacity and current assignment. (E1) 5\. System closes the old class assignment and creates the new assignment with effective date. 6\. System marks the request Completed and notifies affected users with MSG35. |  |  |

## **3\. Non-Functional Requirements**

### **3.1 External Interfaces**

• User Interfaces: SAWP shall provide a responsive web interface suitable for desktop and common tablet/mobile browsers. Role-specific dashboards and navigation must expose only functions authorized for the signed-in role. Forms must provide clear validation, confirmation, status indicators, and readable Vietnamese text for end-user messages.

• Hardware Interfaces: No dedicated school hardware is required for the baseline scope. Users access SAWP through standard computers, tablets, or smartphones with a modern web browser. Printing of school documents/reports may use the operating system/browser print function and ordinary school printers.

• Software Interfaces: The baseline system requires a web application server, relational database, and file-storage mechanism for approved attachments/documents. No admissions/enrollment portal, school-transport provider, grading system, or payment gateway integration is required. If the implementation later adds external email/SMS delivery, that integration is an extension and must not be required for core in-system notifications.

### **3.2 Quality Attributes**

The system must provide a usable, responsive, reliable, secure, and maintainable environment for routine school administration and parent-school workflows.

#### ***3.2.1 Usability***

• Learnability: A new Parent / Guardian or Homeroom Teacher should be able to complete common tasks (view child/class information, record attendance, submit a request, register lunch) after no more than 15 minutes of basic orientation.

• Consistency: Similar actions such as Submit, Approve, Reject, Cancel, Save, and Back must use consistent labels and placement across modules.

• Error Prevention: Required fields, cutoff times, request status, and destructive/irreversible actions must be clearly indicated before confirmation.

• Accessibility: The interface should target WCAG 2.1 Level AA for contrast, keyboard navigation, focus indication, text scaling, and form labeling.

#### ***3.2.2 Performance***

• Normal Page Response: For typical school operations under expected load, 95% of non-report page requests should complete within 2 seconds excluding client network latency.

• Transaction Response: Attendance save, lunch register/cancel, and request-status updates should normally confirm within 3 seconds under expected load.

• Report Response: Standard school-year reports over the project’s expected dataset should normally render within 5 seconds; larger exports may be generated asynchronously if needed.

• Concurrency: The baseline deployment should support at least 100 concurrently authenticated users without functional degradation, with capacity adjustable by deployment resources.

#### ***3.2.3 Reliability***

• Availability: The deployed system should target at least 99.5% monthly availability excluding announced maintenance.

• Data Integrity: Student class assignment, attendance, lunch registration, and request-status transitions must be transactionally consistent and must not create duplicate active records prohibited by business rules.

• Recovery: Application/database data must be backed up at least daily, and restoration procedures must be documented and tested during the project.

• Failure Handling: If a save operation fails, the user must receive a clear error and the system must not display the transaction as completed unless the database commit succeeds.

#### ***3.2.4 Security & Privacy***

• Access Control: Every protected endpoint and screen must enforce role and record-level scope; hiding a UI control alone is not sufficient authorization.

• Credential Protection: Passwords must be stored using a modern salted adaptive password-hashing algorithm; plaintext passwords must never be stored.

• Transport Security: Production web traffic must use HTTPS/TLS.

• Personal Data Minimization: Lunch Service Staff and other roles must receive only the student/guardian fields required for their assigned tasks.

• Auditability: Security-sensitive changes and material administrative actions must generate immutable audit events accessible only to authorized roles.

• File Access: Attachments/documents must not be publicly accessible by predictable URLs; access must be permission checked.

#### ***3.2.5 Maintainability & Compatibility***

• Modularity: Authentication, student/class records, attendance, lunch service, administrative requests, notifications, reporting, and system administration should be separated into maintainable modules/services.

• Configuration: School year, school calendar, lunch cutoff, reference values, and notification text should be configurable without source-code changes where practical.

• Browser Compatibility: The web interface should support current stable versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and mobile Chromium/WebKit browsers used by the target school community.

• Logging and Diagnostics: Server-side errors must be logged with sufficient technical context for troubleshooting while avoiding unnecessary exposure of student personal data.

## **4\. Requirement Appendix**

### **4.1 Business Rules**

| ID | Rule Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| BR-01 | Only active user accounts may authenticate to SAWP, and each login identifier must uniquely identify one account. |
| BR-02 | Passwords must contain at least 8 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special characters. Temporary passwords must be changed at next login when that option is enabled. |
| BR-03 | Authenticated sessions must expire after a configurable inactivity period. Logout, password changes, password reset, and account deactivation invalidate applicable active sessions. |
| BR-04 | Reserved for future self-service password recovery. The baseline SAWP scope uses administrator-assisted password reset and does not require external email recovery. |
| BR-05 | Every protected function and data query must enforce role-based access control before returning or changing data. |
| BR-06 | A Parent / Guardian account may access only students explicitly linked to that guardian record. |
| BR-07 | A Homeroom Teacher may access class-operational student data only for classes assigned to that teacher, unless an additional explicit permission is granted. |
| BR-08 | Lunch Service Staff may access only the student information necessary for lunch operations and must not receive unrestricted student administrative records. |
| BR-09 | Student code is required and unique within the school’s SAWP dataset. |
| BR-10 | SAWP does not perform admissions or enrollment. A student record may be created/imported only for a student who is already enrolled in the school through an external/offline process. |
| BR-11 | Creation and material changes to student and guardian administrative records must be audit logged with actor and timestamp. |
| BR-12 | A student may be linked to multiple guardians, and each guardian relationship must include a relationship type. |
| BR-13 | Each active student must have at least one designated primary guardian/contact unless the school explicitly records an approved exception. |
| BR-14 | Only one school year may be designated as the current active school year at a time. Its start date must precede its end date. |
| BR-15 | Each class belongs to one school year and one primary grade level from Grade 1 through Grade 5, with a configured capacity greater than zero. |
| BR-16 | A class may have at most one active primary Homeroom Teacher assignment for the same effective period. |
| BR-17 | An active student may have only one current class assignment for a given school year. |
| BR-18 | Class reassignment/transfer must preserve prior class-assignment history and record an effective date. |
| BR-19 | A class schedule may not contain two active entries that occupy the same class time slot. Schedule changes must be reflected to authorized viewers. |
| BR-20 | There may be at most one attendance record per student per school day. |
| BR-21 | A Homeroom Teacher may record or edit attendance only for an assigned class and only within the permitted attendance window. |
| BR-22 | After the normal teacher attendance edit window is locked, only authorized Giáo vụ users may correct attendance and a correction reason is mandatory. |
| BR-23 | Baseline attendance statuses are Present, Absent, and Late. Additional reason/excuse labels may be configured as reference data without changing the core status. |
| BR-24 | A leave/absence request must identify one linked student, a valid date or date range, and a reason. Overlapping active requests for the same student/date range are not permitted. |
| BR-25 | Leave approval routing is determined by school-configured policy. Routine requests may be handled by the Homeroom Teacher; cases requiring higher authority may be escalated to Giáo vụ and/or Ban Giám hiệu. |
| BR-26 | Approval of a leave request provides an attendance indicator but does not replace the Homeroom Teacher’s responsibility to record the actual daily attendance status. |
| BR-27 | Lunch registration is available only on school days explicitly opened as lunch-service days. |
| BR-28 | Parent lunch registration and cancellation are allowed only before the configured cutoff for the service date. |
| BR-29 | A student may have at most one active lunch registration for a given service date. |
| BR-30 | A lunch registration cannot be created for a non-school day, closed service day, or inactive student. |
| BR-31 | Lunch corrections performed by staff after the parent cutoff require a reason and must be audit logged. |
| BR-32 | Daily meal counts include only active lunch registrations after applying valid cancellations and staff corrections. |
| BR-33 | Baseline parent administrative request types are Leave/Absence, Class Transfer, and School Document Request. Additional labels may be added only if the project scope is formally expanded. |
| BR-34 | A Parent / Guardian may submit, view, or cancel an administrative request only for a linked child. |
| BR-35 | Administrative request status changes must follow the configured workflow and be recorded in status history with actor and timestamp. |
| BR-36 | A Parent / Guardian may cancel a request only while it is in a status designated as cancellable; approved, in-progress, rejected, completed, and already-cancelled requests are not parent-cancellable. |
| BR-37 | Class transfer approval requires a valid target class or an approved instruction for target-class selection, and the target class must satisfy capacity/eligibility checks when the transfer is applied. |
| BR-38 | An approved class transfer is not effective until Giáo vụ applies it and the new class assignment is recorded with an effective date. |
| BR-39 | Each supported school-document request type defines its required fields, supporting documents, and whether higher-level approval is required. |
| BR-40 | When a requested school document is issued, SAWP must store at least the request, issue date, issuer, and issue/reference identifier when one exists. |
| BR-41 | Ban Giám hiệu approval is required only for request types/cases designated by school policy; routine operational actions should not be routed to Ban Giám hiệu unnecessarily. |
| BR-42 | Workflow submissions and material status changes generate in-system notifications for the affected users/roles according to notification rules. |
| BR-43 | Notification read/unread state is maintained separately for each recipient account. |
| BR-44 | Reports and dashboards must apply the same role/data-scope restrictions as transactional screens. |
| BR-45 | Audit-log entries are append-only for ordinary application users and must not be editable through standard SAWP functions. |
| BR-46 | Only System Administrator may create/deactivate user accounts, assign administrative login roles, or perform administrator-assisted password reset. |
| BR-47 | A Parent / Guardian or staff login account must be linked to the corresponding guardian/staff profile before role-specific operational data is accessible. |
| BR-48 | A deactivated account cannot log in or continue using an existing session. |
| BR-49 | Changes to roles, permissions, user-profile links, reference data, notification templates, and system settings must be audit logged. |
| BR-50 | Uploaded attachments must use an allowed file type (PDF, JPG/JPEG, PNG by default) and must not exceed the configurable per-file size limit. |
| BR-51 | Student and guardian personal information must be displayed only to users whose role and relationship require that information for the current operation. |
| BR-52 | Operational student/class/reference records that are already referenced by history should be deactivated/archived rather than physically deleted through normal user functions. |
| BR-53 | All school dates and times are interpreted using the school’s configured local timezone and active school calendar. |
| BR-54 | Role dashboards and reports default to the active school year unless the user explicitly selects a historical year within authorized scope. |
| BR-55 | Historical administrative records must remain queryable for authorized users across school-year changes according to the school’s retention policy. |

### **4.3 Scope Assumptions and Open Decisions**

• The target school already has enrolled students before SAWP records are created/imported; SAWP does not determine admission eligibility or enrollment acceptance.

• School transportation/private bus management is not part of SAWP.

• Lunch service is modeled as daily registration/cancellation and operational meal counting. Nutrition planning, food procurement, payment/fee collection, and full bán trú supervision are not included unless the scope is expanded.

• Exact school-document/certificate types and which types require Ban Giám hiệu approval remain configurable project decisions; the SRS models a generic supported-document workflow.

• The exact leave-request escalation criteria are school policy. SAWP supports routing rules but this SRS does not impose a specific number of absence days.

• Self-service password recovery by email/SMS is not required in the baseline scope; System Administrator can reset accounts. It may be added later as an extension.

• No grading, learning-content, homework, examination, payroll, accounting, library, or inventory functions are included.
